text: The depot crew raised the pantograph before the first tram left the barn.
A cracked trolley shoe spat sparks where the overhead wire dipped.
Passengers queued at the platform while the conductor counted transfers.
Night mechanics greased the axle boxes under the third carriage.
The fare box jammed after a paper ticket folded in the slot.
Rail grinders smoothed a corrugation just outside the east loop.
An inspector timed the headway between two late trams at the junction.
The motorman eased the controller through a flooded underpass.
Overhead crews replaced a worn ear on the span wire above the curve.
Children pressed coins into the farebox as the tram bell rang twice.
Sand pipes fed the rail when the wheels slipped on wet leaves.
A derailed shop truck blocked the pit inside the running shed.
The destination roll still read Pier after the route was cut back.
Brake shoes smoked as the tram descended the long hill toward the market stop.
Dispatch held the extra car until the crowd reached the outer stop.
A broken compressor left the doors open at every platform.
Track workers spiked a new joint beside the old girder rail.
The trolley pole flew off at the frog and the car coasted dark.
Cleaners wiped graffiti from the clerestory glass before the morning pull-out.
A short circuit in the controller lit the resistor grids under the floor.
The barn foreman chalked defects on the inspection card for car 214.
Snow packed the flange groove and the tram hunted through the switch.
Riders stood in the aisle after the rear truck developed a flat spot.
Line crews spliced the feeder cable where squirrels had chewed the insulation.
The last tram returned with a cold motor and a torn destination curtain.
The guillotine trimmed signatures before they were gathered for sewing.
Endpapers were pasted down after the spine lining had dried overnight.
A dull needle skipped stitches along the kettle stitch of the sewn signatures.
Gold leaf clung to the leather spine where the finisher had laid glair.
The press boards warped and left a ridge in the sewn cloth case.
The gather cooled on the punty before it reached the marver.
Annealer shelves held bowls at a falling temperature through the night.
She cracked the gather off the punty and ground the rim on a wet wheel.
Color bars melted beside a stack of blowpipes near the annealer.
A thick lip formed when the reheated gather was spun too slowly.
The yardarm hoist carried a storm warning above the cliff station.
Cadets practiced flag pairs until the distant mast answered.
A fouled halyard left the answering pennant at half height.
The signal book listed a substitute flag for a missing numeral.
Fog closed the visual range and the mast lamps were lit.
Bark liquor was pumped into the pits where the hides lay strapped.
Beamhouse workers fleshed the hides before the tannin bath.
A sour vat was dosed with fresh tannin after the weekend.
Leather from the hides emerged stiff and was set on the staking frame.
The lime yard smelled of hair and the unhairing machine ran hot.
Molten iron from the furnace filled the mold through a choked sprue.
Patternmakers patched a split in the wooden mold core.
The shakeout crew pulled each casting from black sand after midnight.
An ingot cooled in the yard while the furnace was relined.
Chaplets shifted and left a void in the flange casting.
